description:
FOUND s461ar (agent AR, round 18) by the op/substr.t companion leg, and it is
the residue #911 exposed.  PRE-EXISTING: the write never happened before
either; what changed is that it is now LOUD.

    my @ta = (1) x 10;
    substr($#ta, 0, 2) =~ s/\A..\z/23/s;     # t/op/substr.t:892
    substr(ta_tindex(), 0, 2) =~ s/\A..\z/23/s;  #             :905

perl performs the substitution THROUGH the substr lvalue, so `$#ta` becomes
23.  PCL's `=~` lowering hands `do-regex-subst` the substr RESULT -- a raw CL
string -- so the write site has nothing to write to.  It used to `warn
"Cannot modify non-boxed value in s///"` and carry on (the file's two `is`
rows then ran and FAILED, got -1 want 23); since task #911 that site raises
perl's "Modification of a read-only value attempted", so the top-level form
aborts and the two rows are not emitted at all.  op/substr.t's snapshot row
was spliced 347/7 -> 347/5 with exactly that cause -- a SILENT wrong traded
for a LOUD one, not a fix, and this task is the fix.

WHY IT IS NOT A NEW MECHANISM: `p-substr-lvalue-cell` already exists and
`box-set` already delegates to a magic cell's setter (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
~2245).  `substr($x,0,2) = "ab"` works.  What is missing is that the `=~`
TARGET position does not ask for the lvalue form -- it evaluates `substr` as
an rvalue.  The same question applies to `pos()` and `vec()`, which have the
same magic-cell shape, and to `$#array` under a substr (the case above).

THE BOUNDARY TO PROBE FIRST (perl 5.40.3): which `=~` targets are lvalues.
`substr` and `vec` are; a plain sub call is not (`f() =~ s///` is a COMPILE
error, "Can't modify non-lvalue subroutine call"); `substr(ta_tindex(),0,2)`
IS accepted by perl even though the inner call is not an lvalue, because
4-arg/lvalue substr takes its first argument in "loose lvalue context" --
which is what op/substr.t's own row 354 is named after.

BAR: substr.t:892 and :905 answer 23 under PCL as they do under perl;
op/substr.t's C_ok RISES and the snapshot row is re-spliced; the #911 12-row
table in Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t is unmoved; full sweep (the s/// write site is
on every substitution path).

=== SHIPPED s462at (agent AT, round 19), and the boundary the task asked for
=== was probed first.

WHAT SHIPPED.  ONE table + one recursive form-rewriter + two runtime guards.
  * `Pl::ExprToCL::%MAGIC_LVALUE_BASE` -- the four magic-lvalue heads and the
    base their write-through forms are named from.  It had been spelled TWICE
    (the `\` arm's `-ref` heads and, implicitly, nowhere else); both readers
    now share it.
  * `_write_through_form` -- FORM -> the place form, or undef.  Two families:
    the magic-lvalue builtins (`-lvalue-cell`) and a container ELEMENT access
    (`-box`, the suffix `_elem_accessor` already applies).  RECURSIVE on the
    FIRST argument, which is perl's loose lvalue context and is what makes
    `substr($#ta,0,2) =~ s/\A..\z/23/s` resize @ta.
  * the `=~` lowering: when `_rhs_writes_match_target` says the RHS WRITES
    (it already encoded perl's rule -- never m//, never /r, never an identity
    tr) and the target's head is in the table, the target becomes the cell.
  * runtime `p-arylen-lvalue-cell` (bare cell; `p-arylen-ref` is now
    `(p-backslash (p-arylen-lvalue-cell â¦))`).  Its KIND stays NIL, because
    `ref \$#a` is "SCALAR" -- the `:lvalue` kind is what p-ref/p-reftype read.
  * RULE 12, and it is what makes the head-swap safe:
    `%p-require-writable-target` at the head of the substr/pos/vec cell
    SETTERS.  p-substr's 4-arg form is SILENT on a non-box target, so a cell
    over a non-place would have returned a value having written nothing -- the
    #138 family one level down.  With the guard a declined argument keeps
    exactly today's loud death.
  * `%p-write-match-target` -- the ONE write the s/// and tr/// sites make.
    They used to `setf` the box's value slot directly, which is right for an
    ordinary scalar and REPLACES the magic for a cell (and, for a TIED
    variable, replaces the tie proxy with the string).  A magic box now goes
    through `box-set`; a tied `$t =~ s/he/XY/` runs STORE, as perl does.

THE BOUNDARY, PROBED (5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, 20 rows, 6 SAME before / 17 after):
  substr as s/// target (2-arg, 3-arg, negative offset, longer and shorter
  replacements, /g count), as tr/// target, /r, no-match, m// read, the plain
  `substr($x,0,2) = "AB"` spelling UNMOVED, `substr($a[0],â¦)` and
  `substr($h{k},â¦)` and `substr($r->[0],â¦)` as targets, `substr($$r,â¦)`,
  `substr($#ta,â¦)`, `vec(â¦)` and `pos(â¦)` as targets, plus 18 boundary rows
  (\substr and \$#a unchanged and still LVALUE/SCALAR, the foreach-substr
  alias, an identity tr, a count-only tr, a literal target, a TIED target, the
  #911 capture rows, an overloaded target).  The three that still differ:
  `substr(ta_tindex(),â¦)` needs `sub :lvalue` (a feature PCL drops loudly),
  and the `=` / 4-arg spellings of `substr($#ta,0,2)` are task #960.

BARS MET.  corpus-diff 1 of 111 (substr.t, both sites).  Emission A/B over
1029 files: substr.t + `t/run/runenv_hashseed.t:206`, which carries the shape
in the wild (`substr($munged_seed,-1)=~tr/0-9a-f/1-9a-f0/`) and now agrees
with perl (probed both branches).  Gate-SET scan over both populations (638
files, vs a 4c354bc worktree): IDENTICAL.  Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL
passing 18342 -> 18343, drops 5 = census.  op/substr.t's pass row edited BY
HAND: serial single-file runs give base 347/1 aborting after test 351 and this
tree 348/2 after 353 -- the fix passed its own row AND unblocked the next two,
one of which now fails HONESTLY (the 4-arg spelling, #960).
Guard `Pl/t/lvalue-ref-01.t` 23 -> 30, four of them inverse rows; inverse-
verified on the 4c354bc worktree (rows 24, 28, 29 fail there, the rest pass).

LATE ADDITION, same session: THE ROUTING MUST LOOK THROUGH A CONTEXT BIND.
Found by a probe after the first round of bars, not by the guard rows.  The
`=~` target arrives wrapped in whatever `Pl::CLForm::ctx_bind` put around it,
so only the SCALAR and BOOLEAN spellings were being rewritten:

    my $n = (substr($s,0,2) =~ s/he/XY/);        (p-scalar-ctx â¦)  worked
    if (substr($t,0,2) =~ s/he/AB/) { â¦ }        bare              worked
    push @r, (substr($u,0,2) =~ s/he/CD/);       (p-list-ctx â¦)    DECLINED
    my @w = (substr($v,0,2) =~ s/he/EF/);        (p-list-ctx â¦)    DECLINED

A context bind says nothing about WHERE a value lives, so `_place_head` looks
through the four ctx_bind macros (`p-list-ctx`, `p-scalar-ctx`, `p-void-ctx`,
`p-caller-ctx` -- ctx_bind's own closed table) and `_write_through_form`
descends through one and puts it back.  The declined spellings were LOUD (the
#911 death), not silent, so this was a gap rather than a hazard; the four rows
are in the guard's third `both_agree` table.


s463f (Fable merge review, 2026-09-01): MERGED to main as 6e6f191 (AT worktree rebased over 12eacb5; the two conflicts were the DECIDED/session-log tops, both sections kept).  Fable probes vs perl 5.40.3: #939 19-row file SAME (substr/vec/pos/$#a targets, hash/array element bases, list/scalar/boolean contexts, tr, !~, /g, for-alias, m// unmoved); #934 25-row file SAME except the E-class row (fallback=>1 with nothing to autogenerate: PCL small vs perl big) = #961, pre-existing and filed by AT; #940 11-row file SAME once the probe rows that are INVALID PERL were dropped (a declared sub followed by `/ 3, "\n"` is a perl syntax error too).  Status flipped from pending.
subject: an lvalue `substr(EXPR,...)` as an `=~` TARGET does not bind p-substr-lvalue-cell -- the s/// write site gets a raw string
